title: UK PM Burnham Taps Indian-Origin BBC Strategist as Downing Street Advisor
excerpt: Gautam Rangarajan, who spent over two decades at the BBC rising to Group Director of Strategy, has been appointed expert adviser on structure and process at 10 Downing Street.
body:
• UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Gautam Rangarajan as expert adviser on structure and process at 10 Downing Street
  • Rangarajan spent over two decades at the BBC, rising to Group Director of Strategy and Performance
  • The appointment signals Burnham's push to restructure Whitehall operations after taking office in July
  • Burnham's government already features several Indian-origin MPs in senior cabinet roles

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Gautam Rangarajan, an Indian-origin strategist and former senior BBC executive, as his expert adviser on structure and process at 10 Downing Street. The appointment signals Burnham's intent to fundamentally reshape how Whitehall operates as he settles into the country's top job.

From the BBC to Downing Street

Rangarajan built a career spanning more than two decades at the BBC, where he rose to become Group Director of Strategy and Performance — one of the corporation's most senior leadership positions. He joined the BBC in 1993 as a producer for Radio 3, working across music programming on radio and television before moving into policy and strategy development.

His most high-profile work at the BBC came when he led Director-General Tony Hall's strategy review, a sweeping assessment that aimed to prepare Britain's public broadcaster for the digital age. He was promoted to Director of Strategy in 2013 and later elevated to Group Director, responsible for the BBC's thinking on evolving markets, audiences, and technologies.

At Downing Street, Rangarajan's mandate is expected to focus on how the machinery of government is organized and how decisions flow through Whitehall — an area Burnham has repeatedly flagged as a top priority.

Burnham's Governance Overhaul

Burnham became Prime Minister in July after Keir Starmer's resignation, having secured the support of more than 85% of Labour MPs. His nine years as Mayor of Greater Manchester gave him firsthand exposure to the limits of Britain's highly centralized governance model.

Since entering Downing Street, Burnham has ordered government departments to make "targeted transfers of overarching strategic functions" to No 10 North, a new government hub in Manchester designed to distribute decision-making power beyond London. He has also met with the leaders of Scotland and Wales on devolution, though he has ruled out supporting independence referendums.

Rangarajan's appointment as an adviser on structure and process brings private-sector organizational strategy experience to the task of institutional reform at the highest level of British government.

Growing Indian-Origin Presence in UK Government

The appointment adds to a growing list of Indian-origin figures in senior positions within Burnham's government. In a recent cabinet reshuffle, Burnham elevated Kanishka Narayan — born in Muzaffarpur, Bihar, and educated at Eton, Oxford, and Stanford — to Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence, a newly created post.

Satvir Kaur was appointed Minister for Equalities with additional Home Office responsibilities, while Harpreet Uppal joined the government as an Assistant Whip. Lisa Nandy, whose father was born in Kolkata, continues to serve as Culture Secretary. The government's front bench now includes two Hindu and two Sikh ministers.

The appointments reflect the significant role the British Indian community continues to play in UK politics and governance, spanning both elected and advisory positions across the Labour government.

What's Next

Burnham faces a difficult brief: a sluggish economy, rising government debt, and voters disillusioned after years of political upheaval. His pitch centers on running government differently — with more devolved power, less London-centric decision-making, and leaner institutional structures. Whether Rangarajan's strategic experience can translate into effective government reform will be tested as Burnham moves from restructuring plans to implementation.
